A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Western Dharwars contain a 3 Ga plutonic event that is characterized by the presence of abundant trondhjemite plutons and by metasomatic addition to the gneisses.

the Archean gneisses of southern India are more depleted in Th and U than are the Archean gray granitic gneisses of North America, and that the differences are due to the metasomatically added uranium.
the Archean crust in the Dhar war craton is enriched in incompatible elements relative to that of the Canadian Shield.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the U content of Archean gray granitic gneisses is variable and that it can be increased by metasomatism.
the Th/U ratio of a rock can change significantly by fluid metasomatism, and the Th/U ratio is not a reliable indicator of the age of metamorphism.
U and Th contents in Archean crust can be significantly higher than previously thought.
